title: Decision: the ASCII domain rule applies to every entry's domain component and leaves no port
description:
draft-atwood-mls-didwebvh-credential-00 §did:webvh Profile, Domain: "The DID string MUST match the method-specific identifier syntax of [DIDWEBVH] using only ASCII letters, digits, hyphens and dots. No internationalized domain name processing is performed."

Gaps: (1) Literally, the whole DID string has colons, the SCID and maybe path segments, so the rule must mean the domain component. (2) did:webvh writes a port as %3A<port> in the domain component; "%" is not a letter, digit, hyphen or dot, so ports appear forbidden. (3) Which DID string: the head's, or every entry's state.id (they differ after a portable move)? (4) "No IDN processing" vs xn-- labels: they are ASCII, but did:webvh verifiers (jmap-did-types uses idna::domain_to_ascii_strict) still validate them.

Chosen: the rule applies to the domain component (between the SCID and the next colon) of every entry's state.id; it must be non-empty and only [A-Za-z0-9.-], so a %3A port and percent-encoded IDNs are refused; path segments follow did:webvh unchanged; xn-- labels are validated by the inherited did:webvh verifier (a malformed one is refused; documented limitation). crates/mls-didwebvh/src/verify.rs check_entry. For -01: say "domain component", say whether ports are allowed, and say whether xn-- labels are checked.
